subject.title: Feature: Respect userTimezone in memory file timestamps and naming

question: Should bundled session-memory filenames and `# Session` headers use `agents.defaults.userTimezone` with host fallback, or should host-local time remain the documented contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but changing memory artifact dates is a shipped behavior and filename convention change for users whose configured user timezone differs from the gateway host timezone.

options.title: Adopt `userTimezone` for session-memory
options.body: Change the bundled session-memory hook to resolve `agents.defaults.userTimezone` with host fallback, then update focused tests and docs to make the contract explicit.

options.title: Keep host-local session-memory
options.body: Treat host-local filenames and headers as the intended contract and close or retitle the request as not planned.

options.title: Add a dedicated memory timezone
options.body: Introduce a separate memory timezone setting only if maintainers want memory artifacts to diverge from both host-local time and `userTimezone` despite the config-surface cost.

recommendation.title: Adopt `userTimezone` for session-memory
recommendation.body: Change the bundled session-memory hook to resolve `agents.defaults.userTimezone` with host fallback, then update focused tests and docs to make the contract explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: This person most directly carried the current session-memory timestamp and filename behavior in recent merged history.
